outcome: colonization of Bifidobacteria (B. bifidum, B. breve, B. longum)
cohort: The study included children aged 6-8 and 9-12 months, born via spontaneous labor at >=38 weeks' gestation, who either did not receive antibacterial therapy or required beta-lactam antibiotics.
finding: Children treated with antibiotics exhibited a statistically significant reduction in alpha diversity indices and decreased colonization of key functionally important microorganisms, including obligate anaerobic bacteria and metabolically active Bifidobacteria.
cross-section timing: when children were aged 6-8 months and 9-12 months
